subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these exact 14 third-party action revisions across token-minting, security scanning, publishing, release, and Codex workflows after refreshing the branch to current main?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but choosing trusted executable revisions for workflows holding secrets or write permissions is an ownership and supply-chain decision that automated review cannot safely make.

options.title: Refresh and approve exact pins
options.body: Rebase or regenerate the grouped bump on current main, inspect the privileged revisions, and merge only after exact-head security and workflow checks pass.

options.title: Split privileged revisions
options.body: Separate token, publishing, security-scanning, and Codex action updates into smaller PRs if owners want narrower trust and rollback decisions.

options.title: Pause the grouped bump
options.body: Leave the existing pins unchanged until an owner can review the upstream changes and refreshed workflow result.

recommendation.title: Refresh and approve exact pins
recommendation.body: Rebase or regenerate the grouped bump on current main, inspect the privileged revisions, and merge only after exact-head security and workflow checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to release workflows and security-sensitive release validation spanning the affected surface.
